issues.legal_issue: A later suit seeking relief concerning a transaction already available to challenge when an earlier suit was filed is barred when both claims arise from the same cause of action and the relief was omitted from the earlier suit.
material_facts: The plaintiffs’ first suit challenged one part of a transfer of ancestral family property, alleging that the transferor had disposed of the property without legal necessity and to the family’s detriment.
Before the first suit was filed, the transferor had also transferred the remaining part of the property to the same defendants.
The pleadings in the two suits relied on virtually identical factual and legal allegations, and the plaintiffs did not seek relief concerning the second transfer in the first suit.

The plaintiffs later brought a separate suit seeking to set aside the second transfer. They argued, among other things, that its different limitation period meant that the later suit had a different cause of action.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was barred because the omitted relief arose from the same cause of action and could have been sought in the earlier suit. The appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside. The Court did not decide the constructive-res-judicata issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order II Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a plaintiff must include the whole claim arising from a cause of action, and omission or intentional relinquishment of part of that claim precludes a later suit for it. Whether causes of action are the same depends on the substance of the factual and legal basis on which the plaintiff seeks relief, not on the relief sought or the defence raised. A different limitation period does not itself make the cause of action different. The Court applied the tests in Mohammad Khalil Khan v. Mehbub Ali Mian and Coffee Board v. Ramesh Exports Private Limited, and relied on Virgo Industries (Eng.) (P) Ltd. v. Venturetech Solutions (P) Ltd. for the distinction between omitted claims and omitted reliefs; it also considered Alka Gupta v. Narender Gupta and the principles discussed in Union of India v. H.K. Dhruv and S. Nazeer Ahmed v. State Bank of Mysore.

predicates.subsequent_suit_for_omitted_relief: A plaintiff brings a later suit seeking relief that was not sought in an earlier suit.
predicates.same_cause_of_action: The earlier and later claims rest in substance on the same factual and legal basis for seeking the court’s intervention.
predicates.relief_available_in_earlier_suit: The transaction giving rise to the later claim had occurred, and the plaintiff could have sought the relief, when the earlier suit was filed.

issues.definition: When a later suit seeks relief omitted from an earlier suit, the claims rest on the same cause of action, and the relief was available in the earlier suit, the later suit is barred.
